issues.legal_issue: An exemption order made under a statute that expressly requires publication in the official gazette is ineffective if it is not published in that manner.
material_facts: An earlier government order purported to exempt industries in scheduled areas from non-agricultural land assessment but was not published in the official gazette.
The later exemption notification was published in the official gazette and expressly invoked the statutory power to grant exemptions.
The dispute concerned whether the earlier, unpublished order exempted the industrial undertaking from the assessment demanded of it.
issues.conclusion: Publication in the official gazette was mandatory, and the earlier unpublished order was not an effective statutory exemption order.
issues.legal_principle: Section 11(1) of the Andhra Pradesh Non-Agricultural Lands Assessment Act, 1963 required an exemption order to be published in the Andhra Pradesh Gazette; section 21 of the Andhra Pradesh General Clauses Act, 1891 addressed publication in the official gazette, and section 83 of the Evidence Act supported the official status of gazette publication. The Court relied on Sambha Nath Jha v. Kedar Prasad Sinha and B.K. Srinivasan v. State of Karnataka for the imperative character of a prescribed publication method, and on Pankaj Jain Agencies v. Union of India concerning the relevance of gazette publication. The decisions in Bangalore Woollen and Cotton Silk Mills, Municipal Board, Sitapur, and Raza Buland Sugar were distinguishable because they involved different statutory provisions or publication circumstances.

rule.if: tax_exemption_dispute and statutory_exemption_order and gazette_publication_required and not gazette_published

predicates.tax_exemption_dispute: The proceeding concerns a dispute over liability to a statutory tax or assessment based on a claimed exemption.
predicates.statutory_exemption_order: A party relies on an order that purports to grant an exemption from a statutory levy.
predicates.gazette_publication_required: The law under which the exemption order is made requires publication in the official gazette.
predicates.gazette_published: The exemption order was published in the official gazette.

issues.definition: When a tax-exemption dispute concerns a statutory exemption order subject to a gazette-publication requirement, an order not published in the gazette is ineffective.

issues.legal_issue: A statutory power to exempt a class of persons or property from a levy is conditional legislation when the legislature has made the law and the executive applies it by determining the exemption.
material_facts: The statute itself imposed the assessment and provided that the government could exempt a class of non-agricultural lands from it.
The government order at issue purported to apply that statutory exemption power to industries in scheduled areas.
The dispute required the Court to characterize the nature of the government's exemption power.
issues.conclusion: The power to grant an exemption under the statute was a form of conditional legislation, not delegated legislation.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the distinction between conditional legislation, in which the legislature makes the law and leaves an authority to determine its application, and delegated legislation, in which an authority supplies details within statutory limits. It relied on Jalan Trading Company v. Mill Mazdoor Union, Hamdard Dawakhana v. Union of India, Field v. Clarke, and Tulsipur Sugar Co. Ltd. v. Notified Area Committee, Tulsipur.

predicates.statutory_exemption_power_dispute: The proceeding concerns the legal character of an executive power to exempt from a statutory levy.
predicates.legislature_completed_levy_scheme: The legislature itself established the levy and the governing legal framework for exemptions.
predicates.executive_only_determines_exemption_appl: The executive's role is to determine whether and how the completed statutory scheme applies to a class or situation.

issues.definition: Where the legislature has completed the levy scheme and the executive only determines its application through exemptions, the exemption power is conditional legislation.

issues.legal_issue: A statutory power to grant an exemption for a specified period may be exercised so that the exemption takes effect from a date before the exemption order is made, provided that date is after the statute commenced.
material_facts: A later government notification exercising the statutory exemption power was issued in 1990.
The notification stated that it was to take effect from a date in 1976, after the statute had commenced.
The statute authorized exemptions permanently or for a specified period.
issues.conclusion: The retrospective operation of the later exemption notification was valid.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied the reasoning in A. Thangal Kunju Musaliar v. M. Venkatachalam Potti, which held that an authority empowered to bring legislation into force could appoint a date earlier than the notification, where the date was after enactment. The Court held that the same reasoning applied to the statutory exemption power, which permitted exemptions permanently or for a specified period.

predicates.statutory_exemption_order_dispute: The proceeding concerns the validity or effect of an order made under a statutory power to grant exemptions.
predicates.exemption_power_allows_specified_period: The statutory power permits an exemption to operate for a specified period.
predicates.retrospective_effective_date_after_statu: The exemption order takes effect from a date before it was issued but after the statute commenced.

issues.definition: A retrospective exemption is valid when the statutory power allows a specified period and the exemption's effective date follows commencement of the statute.

issues.legal_issue: A requirement that an exemption order be laid before the legislature, where the requirement provides for simple laying, is not mandatory and non-laying alone does not invalidate the order.
material_facts: The statute required exemption orders to be laid before the Legislative Assembly for a specified period.
The legislature could modify or annul an order laid before it.
The challenge included the failure to lay the relevant order before the Assembly.
issues.conclusion: Non-laying did not by itself make an exemption order ineffective or unenforceable.
issues.legal_principle: The Court treated the requirement as simple laying, without a further procedure making the order dependent on legislative approval. It followed M/s. Atlas Cycle Industries Ltd. v. State of Haryana and noted the consistent approach in D.K. Krishnan v. Secretary, Regional Transport Authority, Chittoor.

predicates.statutory_exemption_order_dispute: The proceeding concerns the validity or enforceability of an order made under a statutory exemption power.
predicates.simple_laying_requirement: The law requires the order to be placed before the legislature but does not make its operation dependent on an affirmative approval procedure.
predicates.order_not_laid: The order was not placed before the legislature as required.

issues.definition: When an exemption order is subject to a simple-laying requirement, failure to lay it does not invalidate the order.

issues.legal_issue: Promissory or equitable estoppel cannot make an executive representation enforceable when it was made in violation of a mandatory statutory requirement.
material_facts: The government issued an exemption-related order without complying with the statutory requirement for publication in the official gazette.
The industrial undertaking claimed that it had relied on the order and that the government should be prevented from denying the exemption.
The statutory scheme governed the exemption and prescribed how an exemption order had to be made.
issues.conclusion: The earlier order could not support promissory or equitable estoppel against the statutory requirements.
issues.legal_principle: Where a statute governs the matter and mandates the manner in which an act must be done, estoppel cannot be used to validate an act that violates that requirement or defeat the statute. The Court discussed and distinguished the observations in Collector of Bombay v. Municipal Corporation of the City of Bombay, and rejected reliance on those observations as authority for estoppel in these circumstances. It also referred to Article 162 of the Constitution in explaining the limits of executive action where legislation occupies the field.

predicates.tax_exemption_dispute: The proceeding concerns a claim that a statutory tax or assessment is avoided by an asserted exemption.
predicates.executive_representation_conflicts_with_: The executive made a representation that did not comply with a mandatory legal requirement governing the exemption.
predicates.party_relied_on_representation: The party claiming the exemption says it acted in reliance on the executive representation.

issues.definition: A party's reliance on an executive representation cannot validate an exemption that conflicts with a mandatory statutory requirement.

issues.legal_issue: A valid statutory exemption notification that operates retrospectively and conflicts with an earlier non-statutory government order governs the same subject and period.
material_facts: The earlier government order purported to grant a permanent exemption but was not made in accordance with the statutory publication requirement.
The later notification was made under the statutory exemption power, published in the official gazette, and given effect from the date of the earlier order.
The earlier and later orders addressed exemptions from the same assessment for industries in scheduled areas, but provided different durations.
issues.conclusion: The industrial undertaking could claim exemption only under and in accordance with the later statutory notification, not the earlier non-statutory order.
issues.legal_principle: The Court held that the retrospective operation of the later statutory notification was lawful. Because the two orders covered the same subject and period but were inconsistent, the earlier non-statutory order could not govern alongside the valid statutory notification.

predicates.tax_exemption_dispute: The proceeding concerns whether a statutory assessment is payable despite an asserted exemption.
predicates.valid_retrospective_statutory_notificati: A valid notification made under statutory authority is expressly effective from an earlier date.
predicates.earlier_nonstatutory_order_inconsistent: An earlier executive order that was not made under the statutory exemption power conflicts with the later notification on the same subject and period.

issues.definition: When a valid retrospective statutory notification conflicts with an earlier non-statutory order covering the same subject and period, the statutory notification governs.
